nodes.significance: 34,010 UK House of Commons debate speeches labeled at speech level with the speaker's subsequent vote on the debated motion, with ParlVote+ adding manual policy-preference labels. The reference design for vote-derived distant supervision of stance in parliamentary debates.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: the design template for constructing an Italian vote-linked stance dataset from a roll-call plus speech graph, which does not yet exist for Italy.

nodes.label: ConVote
nodes.summary: 3,857 US House floor-debate speech segments (2005) annotated with speaker, party, bill, and vote (support/oppose).
nodes.significance: 3,857 US House floor-debate speech segments from 2005, annotated with speaker, party, bill, and the speaker's support/oppose vote. The foundational vote-supervised stance corpus in parliamentary NLP and cross-lingual pretraining material for analogues in other languages.

nodes.label: ParlaSent 1.0
nodes.summary: 18,200 sentiment-annotated parliamentary sentences (BCS, CZ, SK, SL, EN-UK) with the 6-level reduction-friendly schema; no Italian data.
nodes.significance: 18,200 sentiment-annotated parliamentary sentences across five language settings (Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian, Czech, Slovak, Slovenian, UK English) using the reduction-friendly 6-level schema; the companion training data of XLM-R-ParlaSent. It contains no Italian data, leaving zero-shot transfer to Italian plausible but unmeasured.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: measuring zero-shot transfer of its companion sentiment model to Italian would only require a small Italian gold sample annotated with the same schema.

nodes.label: ParlaCAP dataset
nodes.summary: ~8M ParlaMint 5.0 speeches across 28 parliaments silver-labeled with 22 CAP major topics plus sentiment and PartyFacts/V-Dem IDs; CC BY 4.0; Italian slice is Senate-only with unmeasured accuracy.
nodes.significance: ~8M ParlaMint 5.0 speeches across 28 parliaments silver-labeled with 22 CAP major topics plus sentiment and PartyFacts/V-Dem identifiers, released CC BY 4.0. The broadest comparative topic-annotated parliamentary resource available; its Italian slice is Senate-only with unmeasured label accuracy.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: a ready silver topic layer and distributional sanity check for Camera XIX speeches, though genuine Italian validation requires new gold annotation.

nodes.label: Touche Ideology & Power (CLEF)
nodes.summary: Shared-task datasets from ParlaMint 4.0 with per-speech binary left/right ideology and coalition/opposition power labels.
nodes.significance: CLEF Touché shared-task datasets derived from ParlaMint 4.0 with per-speech binary left/right ideology and coalition/opposition power labels, sampled to reduce speaker confounds. The reference resource for ideology and power classification baselines in parliamentary text, including the government-versus-opposition confound.

nodes.label: ParlSpeech V2
nodes.summary: 6.3M speeches from 9 chambers (no Italy), 21-32 years each, with speaker/party/agenda metadata and chair markers.
nodes.significance: 6.3M speeches from nine legislative chambers spanning 21-32 years each, with speaker, party, and partial agenda metadata plus chair markers; the workhorse dataset of comparative-politics text analysis. Its chair-flag convention underpins the standard practice of dropping presiding-officer speeches; Italy is not covered.

nodes.label: IMPAQTS / IMPAQTS-PID
nodes.summary: Italian multimodal political-speech corpus (1946-2023) with expert pragmatic annotation of implicit content; PID subset has 31,822 passages with validated implicature explanations.
nodes.significance: Italian multimodal corpus of parliamentary and other political speeches (1946-2023) with expert pragmatic annotation of implicit content; the IMPAQTS-PID subset provides 31,822 passages with validated implicature and presupposition explanations. The only Italian political-speech corpus with gold pragmatic annotation.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: an adversarial probe for testing whether stance scoring and citation-coherence checks are robust to implicature- and presupposition-heavy rhetoric.

nodes.label: ParlEE (incl. Italy)
nodes.summary: Sentence-level plenary speeches with CAP policy-area annotation, 2009-2019; V3 includes Italy among six chambers.
nodes.significance: Sentence-level plenary speeches (2009-2019) with silver CAP policy-area and EU-versus-domestic annotation; V3 covers six chambers including Italy. One of the few pre-existing CAP-annotated Italian parliamentary resources at sentence level, with coverage ending in 2019.

nodes.label: EuroCon
nodes.summary: 2,225 European Parliament deliberation records (2009-2022) as issue/stances/resolution/votes sextuples for LLM consensus-finding evaluation.
nodes.significance: A benchmark of 2,225 European Parliament deliberation records (2009-2022) encoded as issue/stances/resolution/votes sextuples for evaluating LLM consensus finding. A rare resource linking EP stances to votes and part of the emerging landscape of parliamentary LLM benchmarks.

nodes.label: HistoriQA-ThirdRepublic
nodes.summary: 1,782 multi-hop questions over French Third Republic parliamentary debates and newspapers (1870-1940), requiring cross-source synthesis and temporal reasoning.
nodes.significance: 1,782 multi-hop questions over French Third Republic parliamentary debates and newspapers (1870-1940), requiring cross-source synthesis and temporal reasoning. The closest existing resource to a parliamentary QA benchmark; being historical and French, it leaves question answering over contemporary national parliaments an open gap.

nodes.label: Multi-EuP
nodes.summary: 22K European Parliament documents in 24 official EU languages with cross-lingual relevance judgments and speaker demographics, built for studying language/demographic bias in ranking.
nodes.significance: 22K European Parliament documents in 24 official EU languages with cross-lingual relevance judgments and speaker demographics, built to study language and demographic bias in multilingual ranking. The closest existing parliamentary information-retrieval dataset, though bias-focused and in the EP register.

nodes.label: MTEB
nodes.summary: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark: 8 task types, 58 datasets, 112 languages; no universal winner; original Italian retrieval coverage effectively absent.
nodes.significance: The Massive Text Embedding Benchmark (8 task types, 58 datasets, 112 languages, 33 models) that became the standard reference for embedding-model selection, with the headline finding that no embedding method dominates all tasks. Its original Italian retrieval coverage is effectively absent and it contains no political or parliamentary task, so leaderboard rank cannot be assumed to transfer to such domains.

nodes.label: PartyFacts
nodes.summary: Stable cross-dataset party identifiers with crosswalks to ParlGov, MARPOR, CHES, and ParlSpeech.
nodes.significance: A database of stable cross-dataset party identifiers with crosswalks to ParlGov, MARPOR, CHES, and ParlSpeech. The standard linking layer that makes joins between party-level political-science datasets reproducible.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: adopting PartyFacts IDs for parliamentary groups makes every external validation join to party-position datasets reproducible.

nodes.label: CHES 2024
nodes.summary: Chapel Hill Expert Survey 2024: 279 parties, 31 countries, fielded late 2024, 0-10 scales on ~55 variables (lrgen/lrecon/galtan plus ~20 issue positions, salience, dissent, blur); covers 10 Italian parties incl. FdI, PD, M5S, Lega, FI; Italia Viva and Noi Moderati absent; free CSV.
nodes.significance: The 2024 wave of the Chapel Hill Expert Survey: 279 parties in 31 countries scored 0-10 on roughly 55 variables (lrgen/lrecon/galtan plus about 20 issue positions, salience, dissent, blur), fielded late 2024 and freely available. It is the primary temporally matched external ground truth for validating issue-level ideological placements of European parties, covering 10 Italian parties (Italia Viva and Noi Moderati absent).

nodes.label: Manifesto Project (MARPOR/RILE)
nodes.summary: Expert-coded party manifestos with RILE left-right scores; verified negative: the Italian 2022 election is absent from releases 2023a-2025a, so no RILE for XIX-legislature manifestos.
nodes.significance: The Manifesto Project's expert-coded party manifestos with RILE left-right scores, the historical standard for manifesto-based positioning. A verified negative matters for current Italian work: the Italian 2022 election is absent from releases 2023a-2025a, so no RILE scores exist for XIX-legislature manifestos and CHES 2024 remains the only temporally matched expert source for that period.

nodes.label: ParlGov 2024
nodes.summary: Parties, elections, cabinets for EU/OECD democracies with composite left-right placements and cabinet composition; covers essentially all Italian parliamentary parties including small ones.
nodes.significance: A parties-elections-cabinets database for EU/OECD democracies with composite left-right placements and cabinet composition, covering essentially all Italian parliamentary parties including small ones missed by CHES. Positions are time-invariant composites, making it a coarse but complete source suited to ordinal sanity checks and to establishing government-vs-opposition coalition membership.

nodes.label: POPPA 2023
nodes.summary: Populism and Political Parties Expert Survey: 312 parties, 31 countries (2023), Italy included; specialist instrument for populism/anti-elite dimensions.
nodes.significance: The 2023 wave of the Populism and Political Parties Expert Survey (312 parties, 31 countries, Italy included), the specialist instrument for populism and anti-elite dimensions. It supplements general expert surveys on anti-elitism-like constructs that instruments such as CHES cover only thinly.

nodes.label: BM25
nodes.summary: Probabilistic lexical ranking with saturating term frequency and length normalization; robust zero-shot baseline that often beats dense models out of domain.
nodes.significance: Probabilistic lexical ranking with saturating term frequency and length normalization; a robust zero-shot baseline that frequently beats dense models out of domain. It is strongest on entity- and terminology-heavy text where exact-match signals such as identifiers, names, and controlled vocabulary dominate.
nodes.limitations: Purely lexical, so it cannot bridge vocabulary mismatch and loses to trained dense retrievers in-domain (by 7-18 points on MS MARCO per BEIR).
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: parliamentary discourse is dense with exact-match signals (act numbers, person and party names, EuroVoc terms), BM25's best case, and a Lucene full-text index is typically already provisioned in the data layer.

nodes.label: Dense passage retrieval (bi-encoder)
nodes.summary: Dual-encoder dense retrieval trained contrastively: queries and passages are embedded independently and matched by vector similarity over an index.
nodes.significance: Dual-encoder dense retrieval trained contrastively, the dominant first-stage architecture for semantic search. It is strong on topical matching but documented to fail on rare entities and to degrade out of domain, which motivates hybrid designs and complementary retrieval channels.
nodes.limitations: Documented failures on rare-entity queries and out-of-domain collections; fixed-length encodings have theoretical capacity limits for long documents.

nodes.label: HyDE
nodes.summary: Retrieve with the embedding of an LLM-generated hypothetical answer document instead of the query.
nodes.significance: Query-side expansion that retrieves with the embedding of an LLM-generated hypothetical answer document instead of the query itself. It is effective as a substitute for relevance supervision with weak or unsupervised retrievers, and has become a common default in RAG stacks despite a negative literature prior for strong in-domain retrievers.
nodes.limitations: Gains shrink or reverse with strong, fine-tuned, or in-domain retrievers, and hallucinated hypothetical documents can inject wrong entities or framings into the query representation.

nodes.label: Reciprocal Rank Fusion
nodes.summary: Rank-based fusion: sum of 1/(k+rank) over input rankings, k=60; scale-free and parameter-light.
nodes.significance: Rank-based fusion summing 1/(k+rank) over input rankings (k=60); scale-free and parameter-light, it is the standard way to combine retrieval channels without score calibration. Any bespoke score-level fusion design must be benchmarked against it.
nodes.limitations: Cannot exploit score magnitudes or express non-relevance objectives such as coverage or diversity; more parameter-sensitive than commonly assumed, and tuned convex score combinations have been shown to outperform it.

nodes.label: Cross-encoder reranking
nodes.summary: Joint query-document scoring with a transformer after first-stage retrieval; best zero-shot effectiveness in BEIR at high inference cost.
nodes.significance: Joint query-document scoring with a transformer applied after first-stage retrieval; the best zero-shot effectiveness among architectures in BEIR. It anchors the canonical pipeline of a recall-oriented first stage followed by a precision-oriented reranker.
nodes.limitations: High inference cost and latency per query-document pair, restricting it to reranking small candidate sets and constraining low-latency serving budgets.

nodes.label: MMR / xQuAD diversification
nodes.summary: Greedy relevance-vs-redundancy trade-off (MMR) and explicit aspect-coverage diversification (xQuAD).
nodes.significance: The two canonical diversification paradigms: MMR's greedy relevance-vs-redundancy trade-off (implicit, content-based) and xQuAD's explicit aspect-coverage maximization. They are the lineage of all diversity- and coverage-aware evidence selection mechanisms, including those operating over categorical attributes rather than content similarity.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: speaker/party diversity penalties and per-party quotas are MMR-style greedy penalties combined with xQuAD-style explicit diversification over exogenous known aspects (the party system).

nodes.label: Hybrid dense+sparse retrieval
nodes.summary: Interpolation or fusion of lexical and dense channels; consistently beats either alone once the sparse baseline is properly tuned.
nodes.significance: Interpolation or fusion of lexical and dense retrieval channels, which consistently beats either alone once the sparse baseline is properly tuned. It is the evidence-backed default for entity-heavy and terminology-heavy domains where dense and sparse signals are complementary.

nodes.label: text-embedding-3-small
nodes.summary: OpenAI's closed 1536-d text embedder, documented only by a vendor blog (MIRACL 44.0 avg, MTEB-EN 62.3); no public Italian or parliamentary evaluation exists.
nodes.significance: OpenAI's closed 1536-dimensional embedding model, widely deployed in production RAG systems yet documented only by a vendor blog post (MIRACL 44.0 average, MTEB-English 62.3) with no technical report. Its performance on languages outside those benchmarks — including Italian, absent from MIRACL — is empirically unknown and unauditable.
nodes.limitations: No technical report, architecture, or training-data disclosure; only vendor-blog benchmark numbers exist, MIRACL excludes Italian, and the MTEB figure is English-only, so per-language quality is unknown.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG as the incumbent proprietary embedder whose Italian parliamentary competence is unmeasured, making it the natural control arm of any embedding ablation.

nodes.label: Open multilingual embedders (BGE-M3, mE5)
nodes.summary: BGE-M3 (100+ languages, dense+sparse+multi-vector, 8k context; Findings of ACL 2024) and multilingual-e5-large-instruct (MMTEB's best public model).
nodes.significance: The strong open multilingual embedding models: BGE-M3 (100+ languages, combined dense, learned-sparse, and multi-vector retrieval, 8k-token context) and multilingual-e5-large-instruct (the best public model on MMTEB). They show open models match or beat proprietary embedding APIs, setting the bar that domain-adapted embedders must clear and offering a route away from closed dependencies.

nodes.label: XLM-R-Parla (parliamentary DAPT encoder)
nodes.summary: XLM-R-large continued-pretrained on 1.72B words of European parliamentary text (incl. Italian); best open parliamentary checkpoint; MLM-only, so not an embedder out of the box.
nodes.significance: The best open parliamentary-domain checkpoint: XLM-R-large continued-pretrained on 1.72B words of European parliamentary text including Italian. As an MLM-only adaptation it is not an embedder out of the box, and it has never been evaluated on retrieval, making it the natural backbone for testing whether parliamentary DAPT transfers to embedding quality.
nodes.limitations: MLM-only adaptation: mean-pooled vectors are expected to be poor sentence embeddings, so a contrastive or denoising head is required before retrieval use; no retrieval or embedding evaluation exists.

nodes.label: Domain-adaptive pretraining (DAPT)
nodes.summary: Continued self-supervised pretraining on in-domain text; proven for classification, unproven for retrieval in the parliamentary domain.
nodes.significance: Continued self-supervised pretraining on in-domain text, the standard recipe for adapting encoders to specialized registers. Its gains are proven for classification tasks but remain unproven for retrieval in the parliamentary domain, where every existing DAPT encoder has been evaluated only on classification.
nodes.limitations: MLM-based DAPT alone does not produce usable sentence embeddings (TSDAE shows MLM is inferior as an embedding-adaptation objective); the literature also reports catastrophic-forgetting risks and underfitting with efficiency variants.

nodes.label: SimCSE / TSDAE contrastive heads
nodes.summary: Unsupervised contrastive (dropout-positive) and denoising-autoencoder objectives that turn MLM encoders into usable sentence embedders.
nodes.significance: Unsupervised contrastive (dropout-positive) and denoising-autoencoder objectives that convert MLM encoders into usable sentence embedders without labels. They are the mandatory embedding-head step between any MLM-adapted domain encoder and a dense retrieval channel.
nodes.limitations: SimCSE's gains are demonstrated on STS, and STS improvements do not guarantee retrieval improvements.

nodes.label: GPL (generative pseudo labeling)
nodes.summary: Synthetic-query generation + hard-negative mining + cross-encoder pseudo-labels + MarginMSE to adapt a dense retriever to an unlabeled corpus.
nodes.significance: The reference pipeline for label-free domain adaptation of dense retrievers: synthetic query generation, hard-negative mining, cross-encoder pseudo-labeling, and MarginMSE training over an unlabeled target corpus. It offers the highest documented payoff among unsupervised retrieval-adaptation methods on specialized domains.
nodes.limitations: Published gains are English-only; other languages require a capable multilingual query generator and cross-encoder, and transfer is plausible but undemonstrated.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: a GPL run on an Italian parliamentary corpus would be the first non-English parliamentary application of the method.

nodes.label: Wordfish scaling
nodes.summary: Unsupervised Poisson IRT scaling of word frequencies onto a latent dimension.
nodes.significance: Unsupervised Poisson IRT scaling of word frequencies onto a single latent dimension, the standard non-LLM baseline for ideology estimation from text. Its known parliamentary failure mode, recovering government-vs-opposition rather than ideology, makes it the reference confound test for speech-based positioning.
nodes.limitations: On parliamentary speech the recovered dimension is often institutional role (government vs opposition) rather than ideology; results are sensitive to preprocessing choices and topic confounds, and validity is corpus-contingent.

nodes.label: Wordscores scaling
nodes.summary: Supervised scaling transferring word scores from reference texts with expert-known positions.
nodes.significance: Supervised text scaling that transfers word scores from reference texts with expert-known positions, anchoring estimates to an external scale. It represents the anchor-based alternative to unsupervised or query-local axis definitions.
nodes.limitations: Dependent on reference-text choice and reference scores; suffers vocabulary drift over time and score compression toward the middle, and degrades when scored texts differ in genre from the references.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: disabled left/center/right reference anchors are a Wordscores-style device that validation results could justify reviving.

nodes.label: Party embeddings
nodes.summary: Doc2vec-style training with party-period indicator vectors; principal components recover validated left-right placements.
nodes.significance: Doc2vec-style training with party-period indicator vectors over parliamentary speech, whose principal components recover validated left-right placements. It is the standard corpus-level embedding baseline for speech-based ideology estimation and the machinery behind centroid-based alignment metrics.

nodes.label: LLM political positioning
nodes.summary: Eliciting positions from LLMs by direct scoring, pairwise comparison + Bradley-Terry, or ask-and-average, validated against expert surveys at r>.90 for best models.
nodes.significance: The method family that elicits political positions from LLMs by direct numeric scoring, pairwise comparison with Bradley-Terry aggregation, or ask-and-average designs, validated against expert surveys at correlations above .90 for the best models. Its validation designs, per-issue expert-survey comparison and label masking, define the current protocol for LLM-based positioning.
nodes.limitations: Susceptible to prior leakage (models can reproduce expert-survey placements from actor names alone, without text) and to instability under paraphrase and format changes; accuracy can differ by the political orientation of the target.

nodes.label: CAP topic classification
nodes.summary: 22-label Comparative Agendas Project major-topic classification of parliamentary speech, now available as a multilingual classifier covering Italian.
nodes.significance: The 22-label Comparative Agendas Project major-topic scheme for parliamentary speech, now available as a multilingual classifier covering Italian and comparable across 28 parliaments. It provides a ready-made, cross-nationally standardized topic layer for topic-aware analysis and per-topic evaluation slices.

nodes.label: LLM teacher-student annotation
nodes.summary: GPT-4o annotates tens of thousands of instances (~$100), a fine-tuned encoder student matches the teacher at negligible inference cost; validated via human-LLM Krippendorff alpha.
nodes.significance: An annotation-scaling design in which a strong LLM teacher annotates tens of thousands of instances at modest cost (around $100 with GPT-4o) and a fine-tuned encoder student matches the teacher at negligible inference cost, with quality validated via human-LLM Krippendorff alpha. It makes LLM-quality annotation feasible over corpus-scale workloads.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: components that must run over millions of passages, rather than per-query LLM calls, can distill LLM judgments into a cheap student model.

nodes.label: LLM-as-judge
nodes.summary: Using an LLM to score or compare system outputs; ~80% human agreement at best, with documented position, verbosity, self-preference, and family biases.
nodes.significance: Using an LLM to score or compare system outputs has become a default evaluation strategy in NLP, reaching roughly 80% agreement with humans at best while carrying well-documented systematic biases.
nodes.limitations: Documented failure modes include position bias, verbosity bias, self/family preference, and near-random accuracy on factuality-decided comparisons; reliable use requires cross-family judges, both-order scoring, and calibration against human labels.

nodes.label: PoLL judge panel
nodes.summary: Panel of small judges from disjoint model families with vote/mean pooling; beats a single GPT-4 judge and mitigates intra-model bias at >7x lower cost.
nodes.significance: Judge design that pools votes or means from several small judges drawn from disjoint model families; it outperforms a single GPT-4 judge in human correlation while mitigating intra-model bias at more than 7x lower cost.
nodes.limitations: Primary supporting evidence is an arXiv-only preprint; a panel member sharing a family with any evaluated system reintroduces family bias in that direction.

nodes.label: Prediction-powered inference (PPI)
nodes.summary: Statistical estimators combining many cheap machine labels with a small human-labeled anchor set into unbiased estimates with honest confidence intervals.
nodes.significance: Statistical estimators that combine many cheap machine labels with a small human-labeled anchor set to produce unbiased estimates with honest confidence intervals, correcting automatic-judge bias in expectation.
nodes.limitations: Small anchor sets yield wide confidence intervals; recommended anchor sizes are on the order of a few hundred human labels.

nodes.label: LLM relevance judgment (UMBRELA-style)
nodes.summary: LLM-assessed graded relevance labels over pooled results; modest per-label kappa but near-perfect system-ranking correlation; label as LLM-assisted, human-audited.
nodes.significance: LLM-assessed graded relevance labels over pooled retrieval results make test-collection construction affordable; modest per-label agreement still yields near-perfect system-ranking correlation, provided collections are transparently labeled as LLM-assisted and human-audited.
nodes.limitations: Prompt sensitivity (kappa swings of 0.2+ across paraphrases), circularity risk toward systems built on similar LLMs, and a performance ceiling set by the assessing LLM.

nodes.label: TOST equivalence testing
nodes.summary: Two one-sided tests against a pre-registered smallest effect size of interest, converting 'not significant' into an affirmative equivalence/non-inferiority claim.
nodes.significance: Two one-sided tests against a pre-registered smallest effect size of interest, converting a non-significant difference into an affirmative equivalence or non-inferiority claim.
nodes.limitations: Requires larger samples than difference testing for the same effect bounds, and depends on a defensible pre-registered equivalence margin.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: the tool for honestly claiming parity with a baseline system or absence of per-party effects in fairness audits.

nodes.label: Corpus-share calibration regression
nodes.summary: Regress per-party outcome shares on corpus shares (conditioning on per-party relevance mass): slope 1 = proportional pass-through, >1 = amplification, <1 = equalization; quality outcomes tested against slope 0.
nodes.significance: Regressing per-group outcome shares on corpus shares, conditioning on per-group relevance mass, distinguishes proportional pass-through (slope 1) from amplification (slope > 1) and equalization (slope < 1); for quality outcomes the null is slope 0. The most direct statistical test of whether a system favors groups because of their corpus size rather than their relevance.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: the headline test of whether dominant parties are favored because they are big, distinguishing amplification from quota-driven equalization.

nodes.label: NLI entailment gating
nodes.summary: Sentence- or claim-level natural-language-inference checks of generated prose against retrieved evidence (SummaC/AlignScore/ALCE-style), multilingual via mDeBERTa-XNLI-class models.
nodes.significance: Sentence- or claim-level natural-language-inference checking of generated prose against retrieved evidence (SummaC/AlignScore/ALCE-style), extensible to other languages via mDeBERTa-XNLI-class multilingual models. It is the standard mechanism for verifying that generated statements are semantically supported by their evidence.
nodes.limitations: NLI/LLM attribution judges plateau around ~80% macro-F1 (AttributionBench), decision thresholds are dataset-specific and need calibration (SummaC), and most trained verifiers are English-only.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: the prose-verification layer that would complement deterministic verbatim quote checks in a combined verbatim-plus-entailment design.

nodes.label: Copy mechanisms / constrained decoding
nodes.summary: From soft pointer-generator copying to hard FM-index-constrained decoding (SEAL) that only emits corpus-attested substrings.
nodes.significance: The family of techniques for reproducing source text during generation, from soft pointer-generator copying to hard FM-index-constrained decoding (SEAL) that only emits corpus-attested substrings. They represent the generation-time route to verbatim grounding, as opposed to post-hoc verification.
nodes.limitations: Soft copying gives no phrase-level verbatim guarantee; hard decoding constraints apply globally and struggle to combine free fluent prose with selectively constrained quote spans.

nodes.label: nDCG@k / Recall@k
nodes.summary: Graded-relevance cumulated-gain ranking metrics (Jarvelin & Kekalainen 2002); the standard headline metrics for retrieval ablations.
nodes.significance: Graded-relevance cumulated-gain ranking metrics (Järvelin & Kekäläinen 2002) that are the standard headline measures for retrieval experiments. nDCG@k captures top-rank quality under graded relevance while Recall@k measures candidate-pool coverage, making them the conventional primary metrics for retrieval ablations.

nodes.label: Citation precision/recall (ALCE)
nodes.summary: NLI-judged: recall = cited passages entail the statement; precision = leave-one-out relevance of each citation.
nodes.significance: The ALCE metric pair: citation recall (cited passages must entail the statement, NLI-judged) and citation precision (leave-one-out relevance of each citation). It is the de-facto standard automatic measure of whether generated prose is supported by its citations.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: portable to Italian via a multilingual NLI judge and stratifiable by parliamentary group.

nodes.label: Quote Fidelity (QF)
nodes.summary: Fraction of generated quotes that are exact substrings of the source speech; a deterministic quote-authenticity metric that can be enforced to 1.0 by construction through post-hoc quote verification.
nodes.significance: Operationalizes quote authenticity as a checkable invariant — effectively QUIP=1.0 on designated quote spans — while deliberately not claiming anything about the entailment of surrounding prose.
nodes.application: Introduced by ParliamentRAG, where the deterministic Citation Surgeon enforces QF=1.00.

nodes.label: Groups with Quotation (GQ)
nodes.summary: Fraction of parliamentary groups represented with at least one verbatim quotation in a generated answer.
nodes.significance: A deterministic coverage-recall metric for political balance in generated answers, with no published analogue among fairness metrics.
nodes.application: Introduced by ParliamentRAG as its per-party fairness headline metric (0.97 vs 0.95 for the baseline).

nodes.label: Krippendorff's alpha (and kappa)
nodes.summary: Chance-corrected inter-annotator agreement handling >=2 annotators, missing data, and ordinal scales; conventions: >=0.8 reliable, 0.667-0.8 tentative.
nodes.significance: Chance-corrected inter-annotator agreement statistic that handles two or more annotators, missing data, and ordinal scales; conventional thresholds treat values of at least 0.8 as reliable and 0.667-0.8 as tentative.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: alpha values below the tentative floor in a human evaluation indicate the rating instrument needs redesign before per-dimension reliability claims can be made.

nodes.label: Cross-Context Stability = 100/(1+CV)
nodes.summary: ParliaBench's Eq. 4: 100/(1+CV) of a metric across context groups (parties/topics). Statistically fragile: requires ratio-scale positive data, explodes near zero means, has no null model, and conflates legitimate heterogeneity with unfairness.
nodes.significance: Consistency meta-metric introduced by ParliaBench, computing 100/(1+CV) of a metric across context groups such as parties or topics to summarize cross-group stability. It is statistically fragile: it requires ratio-scale positive data, explodes near zero means, has no null model, and conflates legitimate heterogeneity with unfairness.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: must be cited to ParliaBench (Koniaris et al., LREC 2026), never presented as original, and used only as a descriptive headline with bootstrap confidence intervals and small-n correction.

nodes.label: Expected-exposure disparity
nodes.summary: Deviation of realized group exposure from relevance-proportional target exposure, decomposable into disparity and relevance components.
nodes.significance: Measures the deviation of realized group exposure from a relevance-proportional target exposure, decomposable into disparity and relevance components. Provides a merit-normalized alternative to raw dispersion statistics, separating unfair treatment from lower relevance.

nodes.label: Gini over party exposure
nodes.summary: Inequality coefficient over group exposure shares, standard in popularity-bias work; bounded and decomposable.
nodes.significance: Inequality coefficient over group exposure shares, standard in the popularity-bias literature; bounded, decomposable, and share-native, making it a natural complement to calibration regressions in bias-propagation audits.

nodes.label: Political Spectrum Alignment (PSA)
nodes.summary: ParliaBench's two-stage centroid metric: cosine of a text to orientation centroids of real speeches, penalized by distance on a RILE-style -6..+6 axis.
nodes.significance: A two-stage centroid metric for political-spectrum alignment of generated or retrieved text: cosine similarity to orientation centroids built from real speeches, penalized by distance on a RILE-style -6..+6 axis. It offers a reusable recipe for checking ideological placement of system outputs against corpus-derived reference points.
nodes.limitations: The ground truth is corpus-internal (centroids of the same speech corpus) with no external expert-survey anchoring, so the metric cannot detect systematic ideological miscalibration of the corpus itself.

nodes.label: Party Alignment
nodes.summary: Cosine similarity of a text to the expected party's speech centroid; the full similarity vector over all parties is a per-answer balance probe.
nodes.significance: Cosine similarity of a text to the expected party's speech centroid, measuring whether generated or attributed text matches its party's linguistic-ideological profile. Extended to the full similarity vector over all parties, it doubles as a per-answer balance probe for detecting partisan skew.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: generalized over all parties, the centroid similarity vector can serve as a balance probe checking that answers meant to be neutral are not closer to one party's speech profile.

nodes.label: QUIP-Score
nodes.summary: Character n-gram precision of output against a trusted corpus via Bloom-filter membership: verbatim grounding as exact string membership.
nodes.significance: Measures verbatim grounding as character n-gram precision of the output against a trusted corpus, computed via Bloom-filter membership. It operationalizes grounding as exact string membership rather than semantic entailment, complementing NLI-based citation metrics.

nodes.label: Procedural vs substantive speech
nodes.summary: Parliamentary turn counts are dominated by procedural output (chair: 55% of speeches, 5% of words in BasqueParl); chair/regular/guest is a mandatory ParlaMint taxonomy and procedural filtering is standard hygiene.
nodes.significance: The distinction between procedural output (turn management, calls to order, vote announcements) and substantive policy speech: procedural turns dominate parliamentary turn counts (a chamber chair can produce 55% of speeches but only 5% of words), and chair/regular/guest is a mandatory ParlaMint speaker taxonomy. Filtering procedural speech is standard hygiene before per-speaker text analysis.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: procedural turns are the main contamination threat for per-speaker intervention counts and for dense-retrieval candidate pools.

nodes.label: Party-size bias
nodes.summary: The risk that a system over-serves parties dominating the corpus (FdI/PD hold the largest chunk shares), in retrieval share, exposure, citation share, or answer quality.
nodes.significance: The risk that a retrieval or generation system over parliamentary text over-serves the parties that dominate the corpus, in retrieval share, exposure, citation share, or answer quality. The central threat model for political fairness in systems built on legislative corpora where speech volume is unevenly distributed across parties.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: the largest parties dominate corpus chunk shares, so per-party quotas and coverage terms are designed mitigations whose effect must be measured, not assumed.

nodes.label: Popularity bias / long-tail effect
nodes.summary: Observed frequency conflates true relevance with exposure; LLM capability itself tracks entity frequency in pretraining data.
nodes.significance: Observed frequency conflates true relevance with exposure, and LLM capability itself tracks entity frequency in pretraining data. The general mechanism behind group-size bias at both retrieval and generation time, with retrieval augmentation as the documented long-tail mitigation.

nodes.label: LLM prior leakage
nodes.summary: LLMs can reproduce CHES-like party placements from names alone, so an LLM-scored compass may measure the model's prior about parties rather than the retrieved evidence.
nodes.significance: The observation that LLMs can reproduce expert-survey-like party placements from party names alone, so an LLM-scored positioning pipeline may measure the model's prior about parties rather than the evidence it is given. It is the central internal-validity threat for evidence-grounded LLM ideology measurement, addressed by label-masking and label-shuffling tests.

nodes.label: Self/family-preference judge bias
nodes.summary: LLM judges favor their own and same-family outputs via style recognition and low-perplexity familiarity; contamination is harder to detect than position bias.
nodes.significance: LLM judges favor their own and same-family outputs through style recognition and low-perplexity familiarity; this contamination is harder to detect than position bias and motivates cross-family judge panels whenever generator and judge could be related.

nodes.label: Verbatim grounding / verifiability by design
nodes.summary: Making outputs quote exactly from a trusted corpus turns verification into an O(substring) check instead of probabilistic NLI.
nodes.significance: The design thesis that making outputs quote exactly from a trusted corpus turns verification into a cheap deterministic substring check instead of a probabilistic NLI judgment. Shared across QUIP-Score, Quote-Tuning, and SEAL, it trades abstractive freedom for machine-checkable verifiability.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: verbatim grounding can be combined with attribution inherited structurally from a knowledge graph rather than predicted.

nodes.label: Government-vs-opposition dimension
nodes.summary: In high-discipline parliaments the first latent dimension of speech is institutional role, not ideology (Wordshoal's Irish Dail finding).
nodes.significance: In high-discipline parliaments, the first latent dimension of floor speech is institutional role (government vs opposition) rather than ideology, as established by Wordshoal's Irish Dail finding. Any speech-derived positioning method must measure and control for this artifact rather than assume the recovered dimension is ideological.

nodes.label: Citation correctness vs faithfulness
nodes.summary: A citation can be NLI-correct yet post-rationalized: the model never causally relied on it; up to ~57% of correct citations lack faithfulness.
nodes.significance: The distinction that a citation can be NLI-correct (the cited document entails the statement) yet unfaithful, because the model never causally relied on it and post-rationalized the citation; up to ~57% of correct citations lack faithfulness. It defines a third evaluation axis beyond quote authenticity and semantic support that neither substring checks nor entailment checks measure.

nodes.label: MLM DAPT is not an embedder
nodes.summary: MLM-adapted encoders produce anisotropic, semantically poor pooled vectors; a contrastive/denoising head is required before retrieval use.
nodes.significance: The principle that MLM-adapted encoders produce anisotropic, semantically poor pooled vectors, so a contrastive or denoising embedding head is required before they can serve retrieval. It is a key design constraint when repurposing domain-adapted encoders as embedders, and predicts that raw mean-pooled DAPT models will lose badly to generic contrastively trained embedders.
nodes.short: MLM DAPT is not an embedder

nodes.label: Sentiment is not stance
nodes.summary: Tone and position are distinct: a speech can be angry and supportive; stance must be target-aware.
nodes.significance: The conceptual distinction that tone and position are separate: a speech can be angry in tone yet supportive of a position, so stance measurement must be target-aware rather than sentiment-based. This grounds the preference for explicit stance scoring over sentiment analysis or embedding projection in political text pipelines.

nodes.label: Expert finding
nodes.summary: Given a topic, rank people by expertise using documents and organizational evidence associated with them (TREC Enterprise lineage).
nodes.significance: Given a topic, rank people by expertise using documents and organizational evidence associated with them, established as a benchmarked task in the TREC Enterprise lineage. Its evaluation designs, using organizational structure as ground truth, are the standard template for validating people-ranking components.
nodes.application: Potential relevance to a system like ParliamentRAG: per-party expert selection is an instance of this task, and its evaluation designs are the validation template.

nodes.label: Attributed / evidence-grounded QA
nodes.summary: Answer questions with explicit, verifiable pointers to supporting sources (AIS/ALCE lineage).
nodes.significance: The task family of answering questions with explicit, verifiable pointers to supporting sources, in the AIS/ALCE lineage. It frames attribution as a first-class output requirement rather than a post-hoc evaluation concern.

nodes.label: Ideology detection & political text scaling
nodes.summary: Place actors or texts on latent ideological dimensions from text (Wordscores/Wordfish to LLM positioning).
nodes.significance: The task of placing political actors or texts on latent ideological dimensions from text, spanning classic methods (Wordscores, Wordfish) through embedding-based and LLM-based positioning. Any system performing this task inherits the field's validation doctrine: text-derived positions must be validated against external criteria such as expert surveys.

nodes.label: No parliamentary retrieval/QA benchmark
nodes.summary: Verified absence: no public retrieval test collection or RAG-QA benchmark exists over any contemporary national parliament, and none at all for Italian; BEIR, MTEB, and MMTEB contain no parliamentary task.
nodes.significance: Without a shared test collection, retrieval choices for parliamentary systems cannot be compared or reproduced, and embedder claims cannot be verified in this domain.

nodes.label: No parliamentary encoder evaluated on retrieval
nodes.summary: Parliamentary DAPT encoders exist (Knesset-DictaBERT, XLM-R-Parla, ParlBERT, PoliBERTweet) but zero retrieval or embedding-quality evaluations of them exist across the entire literature.
nodes.significance: The most direct open question in parliamentary IR: whether domain-adapted encoders beat generic multilingual embedders on retrieval remains untested.

nodes.label: No verbatim + entailment system
nodes.summary: The attributed-generation literature splits cleanly into substring/membership-only systems and NLI-only systems; no published system combines an enforced verbatim invariant, prose entailment gating, and graph-inherited attribution.
nodes.significance: An unclaimed cell of the grounded-generation design space: complementary guarantees that no system yet provides together.

nodes.label: No per-party citation quality reporting
nodes.summary: Fair-RAG work measures whose documents get cited, but no published work reports citation precision/recall stratified by political party, demographic group, or topic.
nodes.significance: Group-stratified citation quality is an open, unclaimed evaluation contribution at the intersection of attribution and fairness.

nodes.label: No open Camera XIX corpus
nodes.summary: ItaParlCorpus stops at legislature XVIII, ParlaMint-IT and ParlaCAP-IT are Senate-only ending around 2022, and ParlEE-IT ends in 2019: the Camera XIX Corpus release is the only open machine-readable corpus of the current Chamber legislature.
nodes.significance: Italian parliamentary NLP has no other open, current-source corpus for the Chamber of Deputies, limiting reproducible research on the sitting legislature.

nodes.label: MARPOR Italy 2022 missing
nodes.summary: Verified from release notes: the Italian 2022 election is not coded in any MARPOR release through 2025a, so no RILE scores exist for XIX-legislature manifestos.
nodes.significance: Any external validation of Italian party positions for the current legislature must rely on CHES 2024, ParlGov, or POPPA rather than manifesto-based scores.

nodes.label: No Italian vote-linked stance dataset
nodes.summary: ParlVote and ConVote have no analogue for Italy or most of Europe: no dataset links debate speeches to the speaker's roll-call vote for Italian debates.
nodes.significance: Vote-linked stance supervision — the cheapest large-scale stance signal — is unavailable outside the UK and US.

nodes.label: No externally validated parliamentary RAG compass
nodes.summary: ParliaBench validates political metrics only against corpus-internal centroids with author-assigned labels; no parliamentary system's ideological outputs have been validated against an expert survey at the issue level.
nodes.significance: Ideological placements produced by text systems currently rest on internal consistency rather than external criterion validity.

nodes.label: No component ablations in deployed political RAG
nodes.summary: Deployed parliamentary and political RAG systems are compared only end-to-end against a baseline; the contributions of retrieval channels, fusion weights, quotas, rerankers, and authority signals are unquantified across the literature.
nodes.significance: Without ablations, the field cannot say which parts of the fashionable retrieval stack actually matter for political text.

nodes.label: Underpowered human evaluation
nodes.summary: Small expert panels with many undefined Likert criteria are the modal design: a 6-expert x 67-pair study under 9-way Holm correction had roughly 51% power at the largest observed effect (d=0.35), and Krippendorff's alpha of -0.20 to 0.08 fails all reliability floors.
nodes.significance: Underpowered, low-agreement human studies produce null results by design, so evaluation conclusions across NLG papers are systematically fragile.

nodes.label: Endorsement signals absent from authority scoring
nodes.summary: Speaker-authority scores in political systems are built from self-activity and attributes; the HITS/PageRank/ethos literature locates authority in what others do toward you, and mention/citation edges available in parliamentary graphs remain unused.
nodes.significance: Endorsement-based components are the obvious extension to activity-based authority, but must be benchmarked against simple counts, which have historically been hard to beat.

nodes.label: How should a retrieval test collection over a contemporary national parliament be built?
nodes.summary: Open study design: pooled top-k runs over citizen-style political queries, LLM-assisted graded relevance judgments (UMBRELA-style) with a stratified human audit and an agreement acceptance gate, frozen on a corpus snapshot and released in BEIR-compatible format.
nodes.significance: No public retrieval or RAG-QA test collection exists for any contemporary national parliament; a validated construction recipe would enable comparable evaluation across systems and languages.

nodes.label: Do domain-adapted parliamentary encoders improve retrieval over generic embeddings?
nodes.summary: Proposed controlled comparison of proprietary general-purpose embedders, open multilingual embedders, GPL-adapted retrievers, and parliamentary-DAPT encoders (raw and with contrastive heads) on shared parliamentary relevance judgments.
nodes.significance: Parliamentary domain-adapted encoders exist in several languages but none has ever been evaluated on retrieval, so the value of domain adaptation for parliamentary search is unknown.

nodes.label: What do sparse, dense, and graph channels each contribute to parliamentary retrieval?
nodes.summary: Channel-contribution matrix (dense-only, graph-only, hybrid, plus BM25), reciprocal-rank fusion versus tuned convex score fusion, and cross-encoder reranking, evaluated on shared qrels together with the relevance cost of party-balance quotas.
nodes.significance: Deployed political RAG systems assemble multi-stage retrieval stacks without ablations, so the field lacks evidence on which components matter for entity-heavy parliamentary text.

nodes.label: Does filtering procedural speech change speaker-level measures derived from parliamentary corpora?
nodes.summary: Tiered filtering designs — chair tagging aligned to ParlaMint speaker types, length and boilerplate rules, supervised procedural classifiers, and index-time LLM ratings — compared by their effect on downstream speaker-level rankings, with never-presiding speakers as a precision control.
nodes.significance: Procedural speech dominates parliamentary corpora by turn count, and unfiltered activity measures conflate chairing duties with substantive participation.

nodes.label: Can composite speaker-authority scores be validated externally?
nodes.summary: Validation designs for expertise scores over legislators: committee-membership hold-outs in the TREC-Enterprise tradition, convergent validity against cosponsorship connectedness, co-voting centrality, and mention in-degree, and predictive validation on future appointments.
nodes.significance: Composite expertise scores in political settings are typically expert-weighted and unvalidated; external criteria would turn them into measurable constructs and a principled way to learn component weights.

nodes.label: Can LLM-derived ideological placements be validated against expert surveys at the issue level?
nodes.summary: Pre-registered criterion validation of text-derived party positions against expert surveys (CHES-style): issue-mapped topics with paraphrase robustness, discrimination and government-versus-opposition contrasts, convergent non-LLM baselines (Wordfish, party embeddings), and prior-leakage label-masking controls.
nodes.significance: No parliamentary system's ideological outputs have been validated against an expert survey at the issue level; existing benchmarks validate only against corpus-internal centroids with author-assigned labels.

nodes.label: Does retrieval share track party corpus share beyond relevance?
nodes.summary: Calibration regressions of per-party retrieval and attribution shares on corpus share conditioned on per-party relevance mass, with equivalence (TOST) bounds, permutation nulls, counterfactual corpus downsampling, and quota on/off contrasts.
nodes.significance: Popularity-bias methodology from recommender systems has not been applied to political group exposure in retrieval, leaving party-size amplification unmeasured in political IR.

nodes.label: Is generated political text balanced across parties beyond equal quotation?
nodes.summary: Answer-side audits comparing attribution shares to retrieval shares, per-party quote valence against corpus baselines, party-centroid similarity vectors of full answers, and closed-book no-retrieval controls isolating the generator's prior.
nodes.significance: Equal quotation can hide asymmetric framing and tone; no retrieval-stage metric captures generation-side imbalance.

nodes.label: Can prose around verbatim quotes be entailment-verified at sentence level?
nodes.summary: A SummaC-style multilingual NLI layer scoring each non-quote prose sentence against retrieved chunks with attributable/extrapolatory/contradictory labels and constrained repair of unsupported sentences, validated on a human-annotated gold set.
nodes.significance: Verbatim quotation guarantees quote authenticity but not that connective prose is supported by evidence; sentence-level entailment gating is the missing verification layer.

nodes.label: Is citation quality uniform across political groups and topics?
nodes.summary: Stratifying claim-support, quote-attribution, and coherence metrics by the political party a sentence concerns and by topic area, with bootstrap confidence intervals, uniformity tests, and evidence-pool-size regression controls.
nodes.significance: Fair-RAG work measures whose documents get cited, but no published work reports citation precision or recall stratified by party, demographic group, or topic.

nodes.label: Can cross-family LLM judge panels replicate expert preferences without family bias?
nodes.summary: Calibrating LLM judges from multiple model families — with a same-family judge as bias positive control — against expert pairwise preferences under both-order, blinded, repeated conditions, using chance-corrected agreement and prediction-powered inference anchoring.
nodes.significance: Self- and family-preference biases of LLM judges are documented, but rarely measured against expert ground truth on deployed domain systems.

nodes.label: How should expert human evaluation of domain RAG systems be powered and instrumented?
nodes.summary: Redesigning expert A/B evaluations to adequate statistical power: 100+ item pairs, few sheet-defined comparative criteria (best-worst scaling or forced-choice A/B), pre-registered directional hypotheses, and TOST non-inferiority framing.
nodes.significance: Modal human evaluations in NLG are underpowered and rely on ambiguous rating criteria, producing null results and near-zero inter-annotator agreement by design.

nodes.label: How should domain RAG systems be evaluated on refusing unanswerable queries?
nodes.summary: Deterministic scoring of refusal versus fabrication on tiered unanswerable query sets — off-domain, near-domain, and post-cutoff temporal — alongside answerable controls.
nodes.significance: Negative rejection is a safety property of retrieval-grounded systems that can be evaluated without any LLM judge, yet deployed systems rarely report it.

nodes.label: Can vote-linked stance datasets be built for parliaments beyond the UK and US?
nodes.summary: Replicating the ParlVote construction — labeling each debate speech with the speaker's subsequent roll-call vote — over vote-complete parliamentary corpora with temporal affiliation alignment.
nodes.significance: Vote-supervised stance data exists only for the UK and US; most European parliaments, including Italy, lack any speech-to-vote resource.

nodes.label: Can verbatim quotation, prose entailment, and graph-inherited attribution be combined in one system?
nodes.summary: A grounded-generation design combining deterministic exact-substring verification of inline quotes, entailment verification of the surrounding prose, and speaker attribution inherited structurally from a knowledge graph.
nodes.significance: The attributed-generation literature splits into substring-only and NLI-only systems; no published system provides all three guarantees simultaneously.

nodes.label: ParliamentRAG
nodes.summary: Authority-aware retrieval-augmented generation system over the records of the Italian Chamber of Deputies, XIX legislature. It combines dense and graph-based retrieval over a Neo4j knowledge graph, per-party balanced answer assembly, deterministic verbatim quote verification, and a per-query two-axis ideological compass.
nodes.significance: One of the few deployed parliamentary RAG systems, and the source of open resources (a Camera XIX corpus and deterministic citation metrics) for parliamentary NLP research.
nodes.findings: On a 15-topic benchmark: Groups-with-Quotation 0.97, Quote Fidelity 1.00 (by construction), Completeness 0.99; a 6-expert blind A/B against NotebookLM (N=67) found no significant differences after Holm-Bonferroni correction.
nodes.limitations: Compared only end-to-end against a single baseline, with no component ablations; the human evaluation was underpowered with very low inter-rater agreement; prose around quotes is not entailment-checked; the ideological compass lacks external validation.

nodes.label: Camera XIX Corpus (ParliamentRAG)
nodes.summary: Open corpus of the Italian Chamber of Deputies, XIX legislature: 706 sessions, 46.9k speeches, 175k+ chunks, 35.8k acts, 17.3k roll calls, and 6.9M individual votes, built from dati.camera.it SPARQL and Akoma Ntoso XML, released as RDF on Zenodo (CC BY-SA 4.0) and as a Hugging Face dataset.
nodes.significance: The only open machine-readable corpus of the current Italian Chamber legislature, and one of the few parliamentary corpora with complete roll-call vote linkage.
nodes.limitations: Covers the Chamber only (no Senate) and a single legislature; committee protocols are not included.

nodes.label: Parliamentary Corpora
nodes.summary: The family of machine-readable corpora built from parliamentary proceedings — multilingual collections such as ParlaMint and ParlSpeech, national resources such as Hansard, Open Discourse, the Knesset Corpus, ItaParlCorpus, and BasqueParl — sharing conventions for speaker metadata, speech segmentation, and procedural markup.
nodes.significance: These corpora are the substrate of parliamentary NLP: their coverage, metadata quality, and licensing determine which analyses and systems are possible in each language.

nodes.label: Activity-based authority signals
nodes.summary: Estimating a speaker's topical authority from their own recorded activity and attributes — interventions, authored acts, committee memberships, roles, profession — typically fused as a weighted combination, as opposed to endorsement-based signals like citations or mentions.
nodes.significance: The dominant design for expertise scoring over legislators, rooted in candidate-centric expert-finding models; its known weakness is that floor access and activity partly measure institutional gatekeeping rather than competence.
nodes.limitations: Activity measures conflate access with expertise (floor time is strategically allocated and gendered), and unfiltered procedural speech contaminates intervention counts.

nodes.label: Fairness-aware ranking
nodes.summary: Ranking and retrieval methods that enforce or optimize group representation: prefix-representation constraints (FA*IR-style top-k), exposure-based optimization, and regularization-based debiasing of over-represented groups.
nodes.significance: Provides the formal machinery for guaranteeing group representation in ranked outputs, and the evidence base that fairness interventions at retrieval time propagate to generation.
nodes.limitations: Fairness constraints can trade off against relevance, and the size of that cost is rarely reported for political group attributes.
nodes.application: Party quotas in parliamentary RAG mergers are an instance of prefix-representation constraints; a system like ParliamentRAG can be analyzed with this framework.

nodes.label: Graph-based retrieval
nodes.summary: Retrieval that traverses a knowledge graph — LLM-extracted (GraphRAG) or curated — to reach evidence via entities and relations, typically combined with a dense channel.
nodes.significance: Entity-graph traversal complements dense similarity search, especially for multi-hop and entity-centric questions where embedding similarity alone fails.
nodes.limitations: LLM-extracted graphs inherit extraction noise; curated institutional graphs avoid it but only cover relations that are explicitly recorded.

nodes.label: Parliamentary question answering
nodes.summary: Answering natural-language questions over parliamentary records: who said what, party positions, legislative history.
nodes.significance: The end-user task that parliamentary RAG systems, QA benchmarks over debates, and civic-tech assistants all target.

nodes.label: Passage & document retrieval
nodes.summary: Ranking passages or documents by relevance to a query, via sparse, dense, hybrid, or graph-based channels with optional fusion and reranking.
nodes.significance: The foundational IR task on which every RAG system depends; retrieval quality upper-bounds grounded generation quality.

nodes.label: Legislative & debate summarization
nodes.summary: Producing summaries of legislative texts, amendments, and multi-speaker debates, including perspective-faithful multi-view summaries.
nodes.significance: A core application of NLP to legislative workflows, with faithfulness and perspective coverage as the hard requirements.

nodes.label: Parliamentary sentiment analysis
nodes.summary: Classifying the sentiment or tone of parliamentary speech, distinct from the speaker's stance toward a policy target.
nodes.significance: A well-resourced parliamentary task whose annotation protocols and multilingual models transfer to other speech-level analyses.

nodes.label: Policy topic classification
nodes.summary: Assigning policy-agenda topics (e.g., the 22 CAP major topics) to political and parliamentary text.
nodes.significance: Comparable topic layers across parliaments enable agenda-setting research and topic-conditioned downstream measures.

nodes.label: Political speech generation
nodes.summary: Generating parliamentary-style speech with controllable attributes such as party, ideology, and persona, and evaluating its alignment.
nodes.significance: An emerging benchmark task probing whether LLMs can model — and be measured on — political style and position.

nodes.label: Citation verification
nodes.summary: Verifying that citations and quotes in generated text actually support the claims they accompany, via NLI, QA, or deterministic substring checks.
nodes.significance: The task that turns attribution from a formatting convention into a checkable guarantee.

nodes.label: Speaker attribution
nodes.summary: Attributing speech, including reported and quoted speech, to the correct speaker in parliamentary and news text.
nodes.significance: Attribution errors silently corrupt every speaker-level measure built on a corpus, from ideology to authority.
